voices.instruct: A man in his early forties with a low, gravelly baritone. American English. Hardboiled detective narration: slow, dry, weary and understated, a little hoarse from cigarettes and no sleep. Close to the microphone, quiet, never theatrical.

A man of about forty with a deep, smooth, quiet voice. American English. Flat and matter-of-fact, tired, with dry humour under it; he speaks slowly and lets each sentence fall away at the end. Intimate, late at night.

A Japanese man in his early forties speaking fluent English with a light Japanese accent. A low, rough baritone, slow and weary: a detective thinking aloud late at night. Quiet, close to the microphone, understated.

ref_text: It had been raining for three days. The kind of rain that doesn't wash anything clean. I lit a cigarette, watched the neon bleed into the gutter, and waited for a phone that wasn't going to ring.

lines.text: Kaburo at three in the morning. Everybody awake is either selling something or paying for it.
Monday again. I counted the bills twice. It didn't make them more.
Booth seventeen. A reclining chair, a lamp, and a door that doesn't lock. Home.
She said her husband was missing. She didn't say she wanted him found.
You're asking the wrong question. Ask me who paid for the room.
Megumi. I still look for her face in every crowd. That's the job now. That was always the job.
Put the gun down, kid. Nobody's paying you enough for this.

fish.text: [low, tired voice] Monday again. [sigh] I counted the bills twice. [pause] It didn't make them more.
[quiet, sad, almost whispering] Megumi. [pause] I still look for her face in every crowd. That's the job now. [pause] That was always the job.
[calm, cold, threatening] Put the gun down, kid. [pause] Nobody's paying you enough for this.
